candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12: identify adverse effects and contraindications, monitor medication response, and provide safe medication care.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — fluconazole hepatic toxicity and monitoring
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize rising liver tests during fluconazole therapy as a potential hepatic-safety signal requiring monitoring for more severe injury and appropriate escalation if clinical liver disease develops.

options.A: Recognize possible fluconazole-associated hepatic injury and ensure worsening liver injury is monitored when liver tests become abnormal.
options.B: Assume fluconazole has no clinically important hepatic effects even when the client’s liver tests are rising.
options.C: Ignore abnormal liver tests unless blood glucose is also elevated during the antifungal treatment course.
options.D: Assume fluconazole liver injury occurs only after a predictable cumulative dose and therefore cannot occur earlier in therapy.

candidate.rationale: DailyMed fluconazole labeling warns that fluconazole should be used cautiously in patients with liver dysfunction and has been associated with rare serious hepatic toxicity. The label specifically states that patients who develop abnormal liver function tests during therapy should be monitored for more severe hepatic injury; if clinical signs and symptoms consistent with fluconazole-attributable liver disease develop, the drug should be discontinued. A is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Fluconazole can cause serious hepatic toxicity; patients who develop abnormal liver tests during therapy should be monitored for progression to more severe hepatic injury.
candidate.source_locator: Warnings > Hepatic Injury: caution in liver dysfunction; rare serious hepatic toxicity; no obvious relationship to dose or duration; abnormal liver-function tests require monitoring for more severe hepatic injury; discontinue if attributable clinical liver-disease signs/symptoms develop.
candidate.source_organization: DailyMed / U.S. National Library of Medicine official drug label
candidate.source_version_date: Current DailyMed fluconazole labeling; live-rechecked August 16, 2026
candidate.stem: A client with prior liver disease is receiving systemic fluconazole and develops rising aminotransferases. What should the nurse recognize?
